subtitle: Why Some Companies Win
sentences: Today, I would like to talk about competitive advantage, a key concept in every MBA strategy course.
A competitive advantage is what allows a company to perform better than its rivals over time.
According to Michael Porter, firms usually compete through cost leadership or differentiation.
Cost leaders win by offering lower prices, while differentiators offer unique value that customers will pay more for.
However, an advantage only matters if it is difficult for competitors to copy.
For example, Walmart built its advantage on efficient supply chains, while Starbucks built its advantage on customer experience.
